newsitem.title: CHINA: Technology, tradition leave more Chinese wifeless.
newsitem.headline: Technology, tradition leave more Chinese wifeless.

text.p: Modern ultrasound technology and a traditional preference for sons will leave China with an army of 80 million bachelors by the year 2000, the Xinjiang Daily said in an edition seen in Beijing on Sunday.

Motivated by traditional Confucian canons that place sons in higher esteem than daughters, many Chinese couples were using ultrasound technology to determine the sex of a foetus and then aborting it if it were female, the November 5 edition of the newspaper said.
The newspaper quoted one doctor as saying that 97.5 percent of abortions in his hospital were performed on female foetuses.
More than 118 sons were born to every 100 daughters as of 1992, far above a ratio of about 104 to 100 in 1958, the newspaper said.
Beijing's strict birth control policy limiting families to one child has made many couples desperate to ensure they can have a son.
Some parents go as far as murdering baby daughters in order to win another chance at having a boy, critics of China's one-child policy say.
